title: How David Goggins callouses his mind by facing what he avoids, from 297 lb to a 101-mile race
summary: Goggins argues that comfort kills growth and mental toughness is built only by repeatedly facing what you don't want to face. He illustrates it with his first 100-mile race, where he broke the pain into chunks, calmed his mind, and refused the path of least resistance.

principles.text: Comfort produces no growth; seek the discomfort you avoid.
principles.quote: We don't want to suffer. We don't want to feel discomfort. So, the whole time we're living our lives in a very comfortable area. There's no growth in that.

principles.text: Mental toughness comes from daily facing what you hate, not from theory.
principles.quote: I can give you a class all day long about self-talk, visualization, eat an elephant one bite at a time. But if you're never putting yourself in a situation to actually practice these things, you're never going to grow.

principles.text: Callous your mind, because the biggest fight is internal.
principles.quote: The biggest war you're ever going to go through is right between your own ears. It's in your mind.

principles.text: In crisis, calm the mind and break the enormous task into small chunks.
principles.quote: I had to make this enormous thing small. I have 30 more miles to run

principles.text: Once your mind knows you won't quit, it finds more for you.
principles.quote: once the mind knows you're not going to quit something, it's going to try to find more. It's going to try to give you more.

principles.text: Refusing the path of least resistance unites mind, body and spirit.
principles.quote: My mind, and my body, and my spirit became one for the first time ever.
